news.title: Dividend increased to ₹3.00
news.body: Dividend of ₹3.00 is 3.4% higher than last year. Ex-date: 12th June 2026 Payment date: 20th July 2026 Dividend yield will be 2.7%, which is higher than the industry average of 1.1%. Sustainability & Growth Dividend is well covered by earnings (19% payout ratio) and is expected to be well covered in 3 years' time (23% forecast payout ratio). The dividend has decreased over the past 10 years, indicating a lack of growth and stability in payments. EPS is expected to grow by 9.8% over the next 3 years, which should provide support to the dividend and adequate earnings cover.

news.title: CFM ARC Reportedly Leads Race for Gammon India's INR 5,140 Million Debt
news.body: CFM ARC (CFM Asset Reconstruction Private Limited) has emerged as the anchor bidder to takeover the INR 5,140 million debt of engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company Gammon India Ltd. from state-owned Punjab National Bank (NSEI:PNB). Documents accessed by ET show that PNB has called for a challenging bid to the INR 1,400 million all cash offer it received from CFM ARC for its INR 5,140 million loans in the EPC company. "The bank has initiated a Swiss auction to find a better price on an all cash basis. Bidding is likely via an electronic auction next week. From CFM's perspective, it will help the company to consolidate Gammon's debt," said a person aware of the details. news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹4.83 (vs ₹4.18 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹4.83 (up from ₹4.18 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹146.1b (down 2.3% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹55.6b (up 16% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 38% (up from 32% in 3Q 2025). The increase in margin was driven by lower expenses. Revenue is forecast to grow 14% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 2.7% growth forecast for the Banks industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 53% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 31% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.
